title: Flaps, blinds and a deck of cards
blurb: Four more controls from the ui-feed collection, where the moving part is a picture of the control's own element drawn in pieces: a date field whose digits tumble on split-flap drums, a <select> drawn as a bus destination blind, pagination as a lift floor indicator, and pagination as a riffled deck of cards.
question: Can one element's picture, drawn in pieces with a transform, stand in for a moving mechanical part, and do the elements still work where the pieces land?
result: Yes. A flap is the top or bottom half of a field's picture squashed towards the middle, a blind is one tall element drawn through a window, and a riffled card is a slice of the stack of pages drawn with a rotate and a translate. Only an element with the drawable attribute can be drawn, and the elements inside a drawn picture are hit where that picture put them.
